data.text:
TUESDAY MORNING WEATHER
(Powered By: Rose City Air) 

Good Tuesday morning! First off, our cold front is running behind schedule, and that has resulted in much warmer temps to start the day than anticipated. The front is on its way and will get through here throughout the course of the day, but it will take its sweet time to do so. That’s why you’re seeing the overcast & weak line of showers that we have out there this morning, too.
• You can see the front’s effects, though, with the lower dew points already through Wood County and the northerly wind shift. This will continue to occur as we go through the morning from northwest to southeast. We’ll also clear the clouds out gradually in the process as well. So, even though we’re starting off in the lower 70s, it’ll be hard to recover too much in the face of this invading airmass. 
• We will clear pretty rapidly behind the boundary, even though the breezy conditions will hang around through the end of the day, helping to offset the daytime warming process.
• By tonight, once we’ve lost the effects of the sun, and in the presence of a clear sky, the much drier airmass, and what’ll become a light wind, we should cool pretty effectively after dark to the point where I think we’ll see quite a few 40s on the board by daybreak on Wednesday. 
• Sunshine should take us through the day on Wednesday with a gradually returning southerly wind as today’s invading surface high pressure area scoots off to the east. This will help to boost overnight lows on Wednesday night a good bit over the previous night’s numbers.
• The increase in moisture on Wednesday night and Thursday, along with the passage of a warm front, should allow for at least a low-end chance for a shower that afternoon and overnight. This will also mean warmer overnight temps back into the 60s as opposed to the cooler numbers we will have seen earlier in the week. 
• The pattern will continue to amplify on Friday as a slow-moving trough approaches from the west and helps to produce a better and better environment for showers as we go through the day and even more so by Friday night. This, as I talked about yesterday, should have implications for area football games at that time. We’ll be breezy as well for both Friday and Saturday, for that matter. 
• Speaking of Saturday, that also looks like a price day for rainfall across the area. In fact, WPC already has most of our area outlined with a “Marginal” flash flood risk for that day. Our western counties see that same designation on Friday night as well. Look for us to maintain some decent rainfall chances heading into Saturday night while gradually lowering them heading into the day on Sunday as the main trough eases off to the east.  This should result in a quiet and pleasant day on Sunday.
• As you’ve seen me mention of late, the pattern will not be done yet by Monday of next week, when what looks like another very decent front pushes through here during what’ll probably be the afternoon or early evening hours of Monday. It’ll bring a fresh batch of pleasant air into the region and have us Breezy for Monday night, heading into early Tuesday. I don’t think 60s are out of the question for highs by the middle of this coming week. 

Tropics:  NHC is still pretty hot on that system quickly organizing further down in the Western Caribbean into a Tropical Storm, probably before the end of the day. It would be christened Melissa at that time. The questions then become how much further will she strengthen, and where does she go? It would appear as though she’ll make a pretty hard move back to the northeast, eventually tracking over Cuba or even Hispaniola and skirting just south Florida before it’s all said and done. Intensity models are still trying to get a handle on things, but that should become more concise as it completely organizes and more members are then allowed onto the case. I would bet a Cat 1 or 2 hurricane in this case, at least for now.
